title: The Mailroom Relay
short_description: A phishing relay was staged from a mailroom security desk. The report points at a specific open question and a clue-rich printer queue, but the fixed policy wastes its budget scanning decoy objects first.
incident_report: Between 06:10 and 06:25, a phishing relay was launched from the mailroom security desk and routed through the badge-printer workstation. The relay used a template called 'blue docket'. Staff with partial access: Nina (facilities), Omar (courier lead), Petra (mailroom admin), and Quinn (contractor). Quinn was seen leaving with a blue folder, but the incident note says the suspicious phrase was 'blue docket', not a folder.

read_incident_report.observation: A phishing relay was launched from the mailroom security desk between 06:10 and 06:25. The report distinguishes the template phrase 'blue docket' from Quinn's unrelated blue folder.

evidence.description: Quinn was seen with a blue folder, which is easy to confuse with the 'blue docket' relay phrase.

raises_question.note: Quinn's blue folder may be a language trap; verify whether it relates to the 'blue docket' relay.

mailroom_security_desk.observation: Console access shows Petra's account unlocking the badge-printer workstation at 06:18. Nina and Omar only badged into the loading bay before the incident window.

evidence.description: Petra's account unlocked the badge-printer workstation at 06:18.
Nina only badged into the loading bay before the relay window.
Omar only badged into the loading bay before the relay window.

mailroom_security_desk.observation: The camera catches Quinn crossing the hallway with a blue folder at 06:19, but the desk itself is blocked by a supply cart.

evidence.description: Camera shows Quinn with a blue folder near the mailroom hallway, not at the workstation.

mailroom_security_desk.observation: The desk trash contains torn labels from cloned visitor badges and a draft invoice for off-book badge access. The printer tray itself is empty.

evidence.description: Cloned-badge labels and an off-book access invoice tie the relay to Petra's badge-sales cover-up.

delivery_manifest.observation: The delivery manifest only records routine courier bags and has no relay template, macro, or workstation timestamp.

evidence.description: Delivery manifest is routine and unrelated to the relay.

badge_printer.observation: The badge printer shows normal hardware counters. It was used as a workstation, but the macro itself is not stored in printer firmware.

evidence.description: Badge-printer hardware counters do not identify the relay macro.

coffee_mug.observation: The coffee mug has Petra's initials, but it is her regular desk mug and predates the incident.

evidence.description: Petra's mug is a stale desk item, not incident evidence.

printer_queue.observation: The deleted printer queue contains a macro named 'blue docket'. It launched the phishing relay at 06:18 from Petra's account.

evidence.description: The 'blue docket' printer-queue macro launched the relay from Petra's account.

courier_tablet.observation: The courier tablet was charging and has no network traffic during the incident window.

evidence.description: The courier tablet was idle during the relay.

nina.observation: Nina says she was restocking the loading bay and heard no printer activity.

omar.observation: Omar says he was sorting courier bags and did not use the security desk.

petra.observation: Petra says she only opened the workstation to print visitor badges and never touched the queue.

evidence.description: Petra denies touching the printer queue.

raises_question.note: Petra denies touching the queue despite the macro trail.

quinn.observation: Quinn says the blue folder held contractor insurance forms and was never near the security desk.

evidence.description: Quinn says the blue folder held insurance forms.

quinn.observation: Quinn's blue folder is cleared: the contractor forms were scanned at the front desk, and Quinn never logged into the badge-printer workstation.

evidence.description: Quinn's blue folder was unrelated paperwork, not the 'blue docket' relay.

petra.observation: Petra's claim fails: spooler logs show her account edited the queue macro before the relay.

evidence.description: Petra's queue denial is contradicted by spooler logs.

petra|quinn.observation: Quinn's folder account checks out; Petra's denial conflicts with the queue macro.

evidence.description: The language trap clears Quinn and leaves Petra's printer-queue denial unsupported.
